sections.section_title: Clearing the tim_ocxref signal on an external event
sections.text_helper: Section 31.3.23 "Clearing the tim_ocxref signal on an external event" in chapter 31 (Advanced-control timers (TIM1/TIM8)), RM0522 Rev 1, page 1018.
sections.section_content:
The tim_ocxref signal of a given channel can be cleared when a high level is applied on the
tim_ocref_clr_int input (OCxCE enable bit in the corresponding TIM_CCMRx register set to
1). tim_ocxref remains low until the next transition to the active state, on the following PWM
cycle. This function can only be used in Output compare and PWM modes. It must not be
used in Forced mode. tim_ocref_clr_int input can be selected between the tim_ocref_clr
input and tim_etrf (tim_etr_in after the filter) by configuring the OCCS bit in the TIM_SMCR
register.
The tim_ocref_clr input can be selected among several inputs, using the
OCRSEL[3:0] bitfield in the TIM_AF2 register, as shown on the Figure277 below. Refer to
Section31.3.2: TIM1/TIM8 pins and internal signals for a list of sources available in the
product.
[Figure 277. tim_ocref_clr input selection multiplexer]
When tim_etrf is chosen, tim_etr_in must be configured as follows:
1. The external trigger prescaler must be kept off: bits ETPS[1:0] of the TIM_SMCR
register set to 00.
2. The external clock mode 2 must be disabled: bit ECE of the TIM_SMCR register set to
0.
3. The external trigger polarity (ETP) and the external trigger filter (ETF) can be
configured according to application needs (as per polarity of the source connected to
the trigger and eventual need to remove noise using the filter).
Figure278 shows the behavior of the tim_ocxref signal when the tim_etrf input becomes
high, for both values of the enable bit OCxCE. In this example, the timer TIMx is
programmed in PWM mode.

Note: In case of a PWM with a 100% duty cycle (if CCRx>ARR), then tim_ocxref is enabled again
at the next counter overflow.
This feature is also supported in combined and asymmetric modes. In this case, it is
mandatory to have the OCxCE bit enabled for the channel, the OCxCE bit of the
complementary channel (e.g. OC2CE = X for oc2ref in Figure279) is ignored in this case.

Conditions of use
This feature is intended to support cycle-by-cycle current control loops, typically with a
comparator shortening the PWM on-time when a current threshold is exceeded.
It cannot be used for the following modes, where the OCxCE bit must be cleared:
• PWM toggle mode (OCxM[4:0] = 0x03)
• One pulse mode with PWM active on match (OPM=1 and OCxM[4:0] = 0x06, 0x08,
0x0C, 0x0E, 0x10, 0x12, 0x14, 0x16, 0x18)
• Combined 3-phase modes (GC5Cx or GC5CxO = 1)
• Combined PWM mode 1 or 3 in center aligned mode (CMS[1:0] = 1,2,3 and OCxM[4:0]
= 0x0C or 0x10)
